question: Under which of the following Acts can supreme court initiate International Commercial Arbitration?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 governs arbitration proceedings in India, including international commercial arbitration.
 
• This Act is based on the UNCITRAL Model Law on International Commercial Arbitration, reflecting international standards.
 
• It provides a comprehensive framework for both domestic and international arbitration, ensuring that disputes are resolved efficiently.
 
• The Supreme Court of India can initiate and enforce arbitration under this Act, ensuring that arbitration agreements are upheld and arbitral awards are executed.
 
• The Act has been amended several times, most recently in 2019, to enhance its efficiency and transparency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **UNCITRAL Model Law:**

 
 
• The UNCITRAL Model Law on International Commercial Arbitration was adopted by the United Nations Commission on International Trade Law (UNCITRAL) in 1985.
 
• It aims to assist countries in reforming and modernizing their arbitration laws to ensure uniformity and fairness in the resolution of international commercial disputes.
 
• The Model Law provides a framework that nations can adopt to ensure that their arbitration laws are aligned with international standards.
 
 
 
• **Arbitration Agreement:**
 
 
• An arbitration agreement is a written agreement between parties to submit their disputes to arbitration instead of going to court.
 
• Such agreements are typically included in commercial contracts to ensure that any future disputes are resolved through arbitration.
 
 
 
• **Arbitral Award:**
 
 
• An arbitral award is the decision made by an arbitrator or arbitral tribunal in an arbitration proceeding.
 
• It is binding on the parties involved and can be enforced in the same manner as a court judgment.
 
 
 
• **International Commercial Arbitration:**
 
 
• International commercial arbitration is a method of resolving disputes arising out of international commercial transactions.
 
• It involves parties from different countries and is governed by international treaties and conventions, such as the New York Convention.
